newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan Central Bank keeps bolivar flat.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan Central Bank keeps bolivar flat.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed unchanged at 474.25/475.25 per dollar Tuesday despite high foreign currency demand as the Central Bank sold currency heavily to defend the bolivar, traders said.
"There was plenty of demand, especially from corporate clients and the only supplier is the Central Bank," one trader said.
"Contrary to what we expected, this week we are seeing a lot of dollar demand due to the low interest rates," he added.
One trader estimated that the Central Bank had sold between $40 and $80 million on the market Tuesday.

Traders said pressure on the bolivar was likely to continue in coming days, but pointed to the Central Bank's large foreign reserves with which this demand can be easily met. Venezuela's foreign reserves stand at more than $15 billion.

Central Bank officials have said a recent small depreciation in the bolivar showed the market was responding to the exchange rate reaching the lower limit of an exchange bands system established in June.
"The market is following the band," a Central Bank official said.
